claims.explanation: Fluspirilene is a diphenylbutylpiperidine that blocks voltage-gated calcium channels and dopamine D2 receptors, and its anticancer activity has been linked to calcium-dependent autophagy induction via calpain1-mediated ATG5 cleavage and to CDK2 inhibition. Selectivity may reflect dependence on calcium signaling/autophagy and cell-cycle pathways, with TP53 loss and RAS/PI3K pathway activation potentially sensitizing cells, while intact PTEN or other protective alterations reduce killing.

features.basis: TP53 mutations are highly enriched among selectively killed lines, consistent with p53-dependent apoptosis/autophagy modulation
KRAS mutations appear in several sensitive lines and may increase dependence on calcium/autophagy pathways
PIK3CA mutations are present in multiple sensitive lines, suggesting PI3K pathway activation increases sensitivity
PTEN mutations are more common in least-affected lines, suggesting intact PTEN or PTEN loss context matters; however PTEN loss appears in some sensitive lines too
CDKN2A mutations are enriched in sensitive lines, possibly reflecting cell-cycle deregulation and CDK2 dependence
BRAF mutations appear in sensitive thyroid and skin lines, though also in resistant melanoma lines
NF2 mutations appear in sensitive mesothelioma and other lines, possibly via Hippo/calcium signaling crosstalk
EGFR mutations appear in sensitive lung lines, but also in a resistant glioma line, so evidence is mixed
Fluspirilene targets CACNG1 (calcium channel subunit), so expression may determine calcium-blockade sensitivity
Fluspirilene is a dopamine receptor antagonist; DRD2 expression could mediate direct antiproliferative effects
Fluspirilene induces autophagy via calpain1-mediated ATG5 cleavage, so autophagy pathway status may affect sensitivity
Fluspirilene was identified as a CDK2 inhibitor, so CDK2 pathway dependence may predict response
